generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course applies to the exams and tests you are already preparing for. A revision strategy is how you manage the breadth of a subject when theories, facts, methods and worked problems all compete for your limited time. Planning that time against your gaps, and revising actively rather than passively, is how good students prepare for any exam. Treat what follows as being about your own modules and your own revision, not about study in the abstract.

The same habit reaches beyond exams. Wherever you have to master a large body of material under a deadline, the people who do it well plan their effort where it is weakest and practise producing the knowledge, not just reviewing it. The approach you build here is one you keep long after the exams are over.
